clue.text: Schrodinger's cat, terrified about dispersion of particles

indicators.note: about here means carried around within, so the letters sit inside the run of words Schrodinger's cat, terrified

explanation.surface: A physicist's famous cat, frightened, somehow linked to particles flying apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the closing S of Schrodinger's, takes all of CAT and the first three letters of terrified.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, scatter is the deflection of particles in many directions, a spreading-out of a beam.

clue.text: Rebukes Siberian wearing smalls

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the smalls go round the other piece

parts.note: small is abbreviated S, and two of them make SS
Siberian is used to mean bitterly cold

explanation.surface: Telling off a Siberian seen in nothing but underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Smalls is British slang for underwear; here it is two S abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold someone is to tell them off, as rebuking does.

clue.text: Most suitable time to feed monkeys tea, we hear

indicators.note: to feed means to go into, as food goes into a mouth

parts.note: apes and monkeys are lumped together loosely

indicators.note: we hear says the drink's name is said aloud, which sounds like a single letter

parts.note: the word tea is pronounced like the letter T

explanation.surface: Wondering when is the best moment to give the monkeys their tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Aptest is the superlative of apt, meaning best suited or most fitting.

clue.text: Annoy wife with strong V-sign

indicators.note: annoy can mean disturb or upset, so the letters of the following words are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A husband who flashes a rude gesture to provoke his tough wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Annoy looks like the definition; it signals the anagram of WIFE and STRONG.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the V-sign made with palm inward is an insulting gesture, called giving someone the two fingers.

clue.text: Tailless rodent with 502 bones

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter is cut off the word

parts.note: a rat is a rodent
in Roman numerals 500 is D and 2 is II

explanation.surface: A rat with no tail and an unlikely 502 bones.
explanation.definitionFit: Radii is the plural of radius, a forearm bone, so they are bones.

clue.text: Worms dog, shamefaced figure

parts.note: Worms is a German city, and in German a dog is der Hund
someone shamefaced goes red in the face

explanation.surface: A dog with intestinal parasites looks sheepish.
explanation.walkthrough: Worms seems to be about parasites, but it is the Rhineland city, telling you to use the German word for dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundred is a number, and numbers are commonly called figures.

clue.text: According to Spooner, toff welcomed being supplied with strong studs

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words

parts.note: nob is British slang for a toff, an upper-class person
hailed means greeted or welcomed

explanation.surface: A posh gentleman greeted as he is fitted with sturdy studs.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first letters of NOB and HAILED to get HOB and NAILED.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobnailed boots have short heavy-headed nails fixed into their soles for grip and wear.

clue.text: Religious people censoring love in parts of speech

indicators.note: censoring means cutting something out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: nouns are one of the parts of speech
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Pious folk keep any talk of love out of their speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuns are women in religious orders, so they are religious people.

clue.text: Game or sport involving ball and detailed communication

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the sport goes round the ball

parts.note: RU is the abbreviation for rugby union
a ball is round, like the letter O

indicators.note: detailed here means with its tail cut, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a letter is a written communication

explanation.surface: Someone choosing between a game or a ball sport and a long, detailed message.
explanation.walkthrough: Detailed looks like thorough; it means de-tailed, losing the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino gambling game played with a spinning wheel and a small ball.

clue.text: Clever chap keeping abed, sadly withered

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the clever chap goes around the rearranged letters

parts.note: a clever dick is a know-all, so a clever chap is a Dick

indicators.note: sadly means in a sorry state, so the letters of abed are messed up

explanation.surface: A know-all stuck in bed, wasting away miserably.
explanation.walkthrough: A clever dick is British slang for a smug know-all, which is why the clever chap is Dick; sadly turns ABED into EDBA.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that has died back has withered from the tips downwards while its roots live on.

clue.text: Get the better of team in goalless draw

indicators.note: in means the team's letters go inside the score of a goalless draw

parts.note: a goalless draw is a nil-nil score, written as two zeros, read as O and O
UTD is the usual abbreviation for United in football team names

explanation.surface: A side trying to beat its rivals in a match that ends nil-nil.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to surpass them, which is beating them at something.

clue.text: Security of false teeth is assumed

indicators.note: assumed means taken on board or put on, so the denture takes in the other piece

parts.note: a denture is a set of false teeth
to be is the verb that is is part of

explanation.surface: Someone worried that their dentures are only presumed to stay in place.
explanation.walkthrough: Assumed looks like supposed; here it means taken on, as a garment is assumed, so the dentures wrap around the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A debenture is a bond issued by a company, a kind of financial security backed by its assets.

clue.text: Vicious, regressive Blairism, without originator strangely different

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the punk's first name is read from the end

parts.note: Sid Vicious was the bass player of the Sex Pistols

indicators.note: strangely says the remaining letters come out in an odd new order
the originator of a word is its first letter, which is dropped from Blairism

explanation.surface: A punk-tinged rant against Tony Blair's politics as vicious and backward-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: Vicious and regressive look like political insults; Vicious is the surname of punk Sid Vicious. LAIRISM, after B goes, is rearranged to SIMILAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are dissimilar are unlike each other, which is to say not the same.

clue.text: Barker's regularly backing Djokovic?

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the chosen letters are read right to left
regularly means every other letter of Barker's is taken, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A tennis fan asks whether the dog's yapping is in support of Djokovic.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of Barker's are B, R, E, S; turned round they spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Novak Djokovic is from Serbia, so he is an example of a Serb; the question mark flags an example.

clue.text: Weaselly type, dodgy Pinner mate

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or shifty, so the letters after it are shuffled about

explanation.surface: A shifty friend from Pinner, a London suburb, described as a weaselly sort.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinner is a suburb in north-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: The pine marten is a mammal of the weasel family, so it is a weasel-like creature.

clue.text: Lose temper, mouth twitching, after everything starts to implode suddenly

indicators.note: after says the twitch comes at the end, following the other pieces

parts.note: gob is British slang for the mouth
all means everything

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letter of each following word

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A furious person's mouth twitches before they suddenly blow up.
explanation.definitionFit: To go ballistic is an idiom for flying into a rage, like a missile launched out of control.

clue.text: A bit of a thinker, of unusual brilliance but lacking independence

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the remaining letters take an odd order
lacking means without, so the letter is removed

parts.note: I is a common abbreviation for independent or independence

explanation.surface: A thinker of rare intellect who is nonetheless rather dependent on others.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one I from BRILLIANCE and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain cell is one neuron, a tiny part of the organ that does a thinker's thinking.

clue.text: Loose bowels voided, Englishman likely to run ahead

indicators.note: ahead puts the dye term in front of the emptied word

parts.note: a fabric dye that is unfast is not colourfast and so may run in the wash

indicators.note: bowels are the insides, so voiding them leaves only the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A lavatorial picture of an upset stomach and an Englishman about to sprint for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Loose bowels reads as one phrase; Loose is the definition and bowels voided strips Englishman to EN.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose something is to set it free or untie it, which is what undoing a fastening does.

clue.text: Exaggerate when describing unwanted tie

parts.note: something left over is surplus and so not wanted
a draw is a tied game

explanation.surface: A match report that makes too much of a dreary tied result.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdraw a character or scene is to depict it in exaggerated terms.

clue.text: Don't lose hope! Do I deserve any?

indicators.note: do can mean arrange or tidy up, as in doing one's hair, so the letters after it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who has been told to keep their spirits up wonders whether they deserve any hope at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Do looks like the start of a question; it is the anagram signal working on I DESERVE ANY.
explanation.definitionFit: Never say die is a stock exhortation to keep going and not give up.

clue.text: Making children squeal, I run inside

indicators.note: inside puts the second pair of pieces within the first

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing, the same as to squeal
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A parent's children shriek as the speaker dashes indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: Squeal and sing both mean inform on someone to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Siring is fathering offspring, the male part of producing young.

clue.text: Scoff jokingly, aloud

indicators.note: aloud signals that the phrase is spoken, and the spoken form is spelt another way

parts.note: something said jokingly is said in jest

explanation.surface: Someone mocking another person in a teasing, joking voice.
explanation.walkthrough: Scoff looks like mock; it is the eating sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff food is British slang for eating it greedily, and to ingest is to take food in.

clue.text: Suspicious as wife travels eastward by unexpected route

indicators.note: on a map east is to the right, so the letter shifts rightwards along the word

parts.note: wary means suspicious or cautious

explanation.surface: A wary husband watches as his wife heads east by some odd route.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer east is to the right: W moves one place right in WARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans that go awry go off course, departing from the intended path.

clue.text: Wave of excessive euphoria, dropping E's

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall, so every E is let go from the phrase

parts.note: undue means excessive or more than warranted
elation is a feeling of euphoria
the E's are the letter E in plural, both of them here

explanation.surface: A rush of over-the-top joy, perhaps from dropping ecstasy pills.
explanation.walkthrough: E's is slang for ecstasy tablets, which suits euphoria; here it means the letter E, both of them.
explanation.definitionFit: An undulation is a wavelike motion or a single rise and fall, like a wave.

clue.text: Unhappy pups let off leads

indicators.note: off leads means each word loses its lead, its first letter

explanation.surface: Puppies let off their leads and now looking miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: Leads looks like dog leashes; it means first letters, so PUPS and LET each lose theirs.
explanation.definitionFit: Upset is a synonym of unhappy, describing someone distressed or troubled.

clue.text: Sentence, one foot in length, cut by two thirds

indicators.note: in places the two short pieces within the shortened word
cut by two thirds means four of its six letters are removed, leaving its first third

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A sentence reduced to a third, as if a judge measured it out in feet.
explanation.walkthrough: Length is cut to its first third, LE, and I plus F go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A life sentence imprisons someone for the rest of their days, so a court's sentence can be life.

clue.text: Senior going back in time machine, arriving late

indicators.note: in puts the turned-round abbreviation inside the time machine

parts.note: the TARDIS is the time machine in the British TV series Doctor Who

indicators.note: going back means the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: Sen is an abbreviation for senior

explanation.surface: An old person time travelling backwards, yet still showing up late.
explanation.walkthrough: The TARDIS is the police-box time machine of the British TV show Doctor Who; going back turns SEN into NES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardiness is lateness, the habit or fact of turning up after the expected time.

clue.text: Your old, watery eyes expressing agreement

parts.note: a watery drink or soup is thin

indicators.note: expressing means squeezing out, as juice is expressed, so the agreement is pressed out of the word

parts.note: yes expresses agreement

explanation.surface: An old person's watery eyes show that they agree.
explanation.walkthrough: Expressing looks like showing; it means squeezing out. Pressing YES from EYES leaves E.
explanation.definitionFit: Thine is the archaic form of yours, as in thine own self, so old marks it as dated.

clue.text: Naked, slippery creature said to be Roosevelt's baby

indicators.note: said to be means spoken aloud the phrase sounds like the answer

parts.note: naked gives nude and a slippery creature is an eel, which together are said as nude eel

explanation.surface: A newborn of the Roosevelt family, bare and wriggly.
explanation.definitionFit: Franklin Roosevelt launched the New Deal programme in the 1930s, so it was his creation.

clue.text: Knit unobserved — one of the Queen's jobs for this evening

indicators.note: unobserved means out of sight, so that letter goes missing from the phrase

parts.note: the monarch's duties include conferring knighthoods, that is, to knight someone
K is the knitting-pattern abbreviation for knit

explanation.surface: Knitting quietly while the Queen dubs knights at an investiture this evening.
explanation.walkthrough: K is also silent in knight and knit, which suits unobserved.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight refers to the coming night, the same period as this evening.
